findings.title: Runtime validation skips page congruence for p_align0/1
findings.explanation: The new generic load checker checks offset/address congruence only when p_align>1. gABI7.1 independently requires p_offset and p_vaddr congruent modulo page size. A linker-produced ARM64 fixture modified to first LOAD p_align=1,p_offset=0,p_vaddr=1 is accepted by validate_elf(gui=False), although it is incongruent for4/16/64KiB Linux pages. This is a remaining validation gap, not a newly introduced rejection regression or an observed native crash.
findings.required_change: Test and reject incompatible runtime LOAD address/file-offset mapping even for p_align0/1 (a conservative4KiB Linux ARM minimum can be documented independently of measured kernel size), while preserving the valid low-alignment runtime cases and stricter GUI16KiB policy. Alternatively explicitly narrow the supported verifier claim and keep this source slice open.

independent_tests.source: copied immutable source packet, with original unchanged toolchain pin support file

limitations: No application build or native ARM execution performed.
SDK, CPU availability, native page-size/loader, GUI/media qualification and full gate acceptance remain separate.
ECC approval applies to its exact source packet and does not override this independent reviewer finding.
